implemented: Linux native Claude and Codex launch through one per-profile registry, including configured instances, discovery and quota probes.

Server browsers use the same profile registry with unowned collecting scopes, preserve CDP descriptors 3/4, and await scope cleanup on actor exit. File descriptors are owned on every launch error/cancellation path.

Resource discovery is awaited before synchronous PTY locks; invalid requests do not initialize policy. The subreaper preserves wrapper argv and prepares all CString buffers before fork.

Restarted profile cleanup stops only that profile; another profile remains running.
CDP pipes survive the real systemd wrapper; browser OOM score and owned slice match, another tab survives a sibling close, and final shutdown reaps the process.

Normal and managed PTYs retain PID/session/group identity, controlling TTY, clean literal environment, OOM score800 and the general agents slice. Terminal API launch lazily initializes resources, empty runtime falls back, and owned-profile orphan cleanup leaves the PTYs alive.
